items.text: Whistle at Dawn
Rainforest, five hours before Janardhan's capture—

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Here. You must be dying of thirst.
She lifts the canteen and pours water into the boy's mouth, his hands still tied tight.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: *splutter*
The boy gulps it down fast, but the canteen is snatched away.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Keep that for us! Don't waste it on him!

items.speaker: Student
items.text: *sob*

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Don't start with me! Remember, I didn't ask you to tag along. You were the one that wouldn't leave. Now we're here. Like what you see?
Janardhan grabs the boy's hair, jerking his head up.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Move it, kid! There might still be a chance to get out of here before the circle to the other side of the jungle.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: We cross that river and put some distance behind us, then we'll lose them for good.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: But we've still got to hack our way through this bug-infested jungle before we ever see a road.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Promise me ... once we cross this river, we let him go?
Janardhan stops in his tracks.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Do I need to repeat myself? You can leave anytime you want. Go ahead.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: In fact, I really don't want anything to do with you. So, how about you do both of us a favor and stay out of my way!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: But this little runt isn't going anywhere. I know his kind. He won't just let this go.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: I-I ... I swear I won't tell them anything!

items.speaker: Student
items.text: Just run!

items.speaker: Student
items.text: Leave me here, please!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: No, brat. You're coming with me. You were the one that wanted to find me, weren't you?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Well done. You've found me. All by yourself, happy now?
He slaps the boy's head from behind with a rough palm.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Please, Janardhan, let him go. It won't do any good to drag him along with us.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: If we don't, they'll just have one more thing to pin on you.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Ha! Pin it on me? You think they're only looking for me now? They've already made up their minds!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: They'll beat us both to a pulp, bury us under a pile of fake crimes, and call it justice!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: So how about you stop worrying about me and start worrying about yourself! If you don't believe me, go ahead, run back and find out.
She's never seen Janardhan like this before.
His face is twisted, almost monstrous.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hm?
She notices a sharp stone suddenly appear in the boy's bound hands.
He had picked it up, likely when he fell before.
The boy catches her gaze and offers a look of desperation.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: Please, don't say anything.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Janardhan!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: What now? Do I need to kick you like some lost puppy to get you to finally leave?
She takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: We need to rest for a bit. The river's right ahead.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: If we try to cross it without a plan, the current will sweep us all away before we even reach the middle!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: We should check the water first. Who knows how deep it could be?
He hesitates, then nods in agreement.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Stay put. I'll check the water.
He moves toward the edge of the river. Eyes darting, breath still heaving in his chest.
He takes a soft but certain step into the water, feeling the current against his legs.
Then he looks across to the far bank, measuring the distance.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: The current's not too bad, but we'll need a rope!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Gotta cut some vines for that.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Hey ... you two!
He turns back and sees only Kanjira.
He scans the brush, catching sight of the boy as he runs back into the dense forest.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Ah! I'm a damned fool.
He pulls out his gun and fires a warning shot high into the air.
The first of three.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: *weep*
A bullet whistles through the sky. The boy freezes.
Janardhan lowers his gun and strides over, grabbing a rotten branch off the ground.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Janardhan! Stop it. Just let us go. I'll stay behind with him. We'll tell them that you disappeared.
She grabs his arm and pulls hard, trying to stop him from moving forward.
Janardhan hesitates for a moment, then shakes her off coldly.
She staggers to her feet only to catch a heavy blow from the back of his hand.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Ugh!
She collapses to the ground, the taste of blood rising in her mouth, crisp metallic scents filling her nose.
Janardhan's eyes are cold as he stares back at her. Empty and unrecognizable.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Heh, you still don't get it, do you, kid? You still think you can make this work.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Haven't you figured out yet what your kindness gets you?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: You think it will change things, but it won't; all it does is let other people walk all over you.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: He shouldn't be dragged into this!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I ... I know you've given everything you had to people, and all it brought you was pain ... I know something inside of you is broken, and you hate this world ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I don't know what you've been through, but I know it must have been awful. I know you don't want to care anymore, and maybe I can't change that.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But ... maybe things aren't as hopeless as you think. All I know is, if you're really going to take this kid hostage, then you'll be as bad as they say you are!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I don't think you want to hurt us. I know that's not you. That can't be you!
There's no shift in his empty eyes as he laughs. It's a venomous and sickly sort of laugh.
Then, he turns toward the boy still frozen in fear.
He raises the thick branch, ready to swing it down on the boy.
*thud*
The second of three shots.
Birds scatter into the sky.
He sways to the side, revealing the boy lying on the ground.
And blood seeps from a fresh wound.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: You little pickpocket ...
He collapses to his knees.
She trembles, her hands aching from the kick of the gun.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm sorry. Janardhan, I'm so sorry.
She rushes over and guides him over to a nearby tree.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I didn't know what to do! I didn't know how to stop this.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Heh, you might make for an even better marksman than a pickpocket. *cough*

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry!
She presses her small hands against the wound, but the blood keeps flowing.
Janardhan sighs deeply, staring up at the sky.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *cough* Listen to me. You did the right thing, kid—You hear me? You did the right thing.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: I wasn't thinking straight. You're right. That kid's innocent.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: I'm glad you ended this before it went any further.
Footsteps close in from the distance.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Y-you weren't really going to hit him, were you?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *cough* Still think you can figure me out, don't you?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: No time left for that. You have to go now.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm not leaving! I'm staying here with you!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Your parents are out there waiting for you.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Then we have to leave together!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: *cough* No ... No!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Come on, please. You can lean on me!
She tries to lift him, gritting her teeth, but he pushes her away.
He reaches into his bag.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Take this.
He presses a heavy leather pouch into her arms.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Promise me. Use what's inside. Keep moving.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Keep going until you find what you're looking for, until you find your answer.
He shoves her hands away and pushes her toward the river.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But what about you?!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: No, what are you doing?!
He's gotten the gun from her again. He waves her away, leaving her with no other option.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: It's time to end this.
He raises the gun toward the sky and pulls the trigger.
The third shot.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Over there! The shot came from over there!

items.speaker: Dog
items.text: Woof woof!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Now, you won't look back.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Run! Get the hell out of here!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: If you don't want everything you've done to be for nothing, if you don't want this journey to mean nothing—run!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Trust me. Once they're gone, circle back toward the station.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Then, keep running.
The police dogs close in.
She wipes her tears and starts to move.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I promise you, Janardhan!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'll find Batia! I'll come back for you! You'll be okay; you have to be!

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Just get the hell out of here!
She wipes her tears with her sleeve before finally forcing her legs to move again.
In the distance, a train whistle cuts through the air.
Her figure melts into the jungle, swallowed by the trees.
The dogs are getting closer.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Heh ...

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: That's my girl.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: Janardhan, you need to know something. A pair of elderly folks came to see me at the camp earlier.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: They recognized the girl. They know her name and where she comes from.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: You're saying they're her parents?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Then why the hell didn't they come see her themselves?!
She doesn't show blame in her eyes, only the kind of calm that comes from carrying too much regret.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: It's not that simple. They're in a lot of trouble now, and they can't risk dragging a child into it.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: Maybe that isn't the right thing to do. Maybe they'll regret it. But I will respect their wishes.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: Listen, I can't tell you more, but you need to understand—seeking the truth will cost far more than you imagine.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: You need to convince her to turn back. There's nothing for her out there.
The man stands, defiant.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: I'm not doing that.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: She's stronger than you think. And this—this is her journey.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: What she's searching for is bigger than any answer you people can offer.

items.speaker: Batia
items.text: But it's pointless.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: It's nothing close to that, Batia.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: There's more to this world than what you're willing to see.
A train whistle slices through the morning mist. The wind howls. Black smoke rolls over the treetops.
At the end of the train, a small hand grips the rear guardrail.
The train picks up speed. The tracks rattle. Birds scatter from the trees.
Newborn sunlight streams through as the train bursts out of the tunnel, flooding the world in light.
